notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Isaiah 11, because I wasn't able to read any of the sources.

I tried to open seven pages at once: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, the NET Bible notes, and New Advent. That went over the tool's usage limit, so none of the pages loaded. A second try was blocked too, and I can't make any more tool calls in this turn.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any notes from memory, since none of them could be backed by a page I'd read.

If you send the request again, I'll start over and open the pages a few at a time to stay under the limit. I'll begin with:

- **Traditional reading (verse by verse):** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/isaiah-11/, Bible Hub (Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary on Isaiah 11) and preceptaustin.org.
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:** mainly vv. 6–9 and 11–16, where views differ on a literal future kingdom versus a spiritual or church-age reading. Sources would include gotquestions.org, ligonier.org, desiringgod.org, gty.org, samstorms.org and wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's notes).
- **Other views:** netbible.org notes on Isaiah 11, and Catholic teaching on the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit from v. 2 (newadvent.org, catholic.com), plus any Orthodox reading I can find on oca.org.

Then I'll write the notes verse by verse, with a URL for each point, and leave out anything I can't find.
